blocks.text: Mastering the Slack desktop app on your Mac

The Slack app on your Mac is the hub for your team. You likely spend hours toggling between your Electronic Health Record system and Slack. The key to speed is keeping your hands on the keyboard. Press Command + K to open the quick switcher. This allows you to jump to any patient-specific channel or private message without using your mouse. If your app feels slow, go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This is the most common fix for performance issues in the desktop version.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for medical receptionists

items: Command + /: Opens the full list of keyboard shortcuts for quick reference.
Shift + Enter: Adds a new line to your message instead of sending it.
Command + B: Bolds text to highlight urgent patient information.
Command + I: Italicizes text for emphasis in your internal notes.
Command + Comma: Opens your Slack preferences to adjust notification sounds.

blocks.text: Medical offices generate a high volume of messages. Use public channels for general office updates and private channels for sensitive patient data. Always ensure your workspace complies with your practice privacy policies. If a channel becomes too noisy, you can mute it by right-clicking the channel name and selecting Mute. This keeps your sidebar clean while ensuring you do not miss critical alerts.
Using Lazur to manage your Slack workflow

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you move faster. Hold Option + Command to ask Lazur about anything on your screen. If you are stuck in a complex thread, ask Lazur to summarize the conversation out loud. You can also use Lazur to dictate messages. Hold the fn key to start dictation. It will format your text cleanly at the cursor so you can respond to team members while you are busy with patient check-ins.

Sometimes notifications stop working. Check your system settings to ensure Slack has permission to send alerts. If you need to focus on a patient, use the /dnd command to pause notifications for a set time. This helps you avoid distractions during high-traffic hours. If you need to find a specific message from earlier, use the search modifiers. Type from:@name or in:#channel to narrow your results quickly.
Integrating Slack with your medical practice tools

Many medical receptionists use tools like MacPractice or web-based EHRs. If your EHR supports Slack notifications, set them up to get alerts for new patient registrations or appointment changes. Keep your Slack app in your Dock for instant access. If you use web-based apps, consider using a tool like WebCatalog to turn them into dedicated desktop apps. This prevents your browser tabs from getting cluttered and keeps your workflow organized.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to click buttons in Slack?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not click buttons or operate Slack for you. It can point to buttons or guide you through steps, but you perform the actual clicks.

faq.question: Does Slack for Mac require a specific version of macOS?
faq.answer: Yes, Slack currently requires macOS 14 Sonoma or above for the latest supported versions.

faq.question: How do I find my Slack keyboard shortcuts?
faq.answer: Press Command + / inside the Slack desktop app to open the cheat sheet.

faq.question: What is the best way to switch channels quickly?
faq.answer: Press Command + K to open the quick switcher and type the name of the channel you want to jump to.
